book_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: What free cash flow and margin trajectory does $53.61 price in, and does ABM clear our 1.50:1 reward-to-risk hurdle once Pass 1 balance-sheet forensics are included?

epigraph.quote: A low forward earnings multiple on an indebted roll-up is rarely free. Always verify what the cash flow statement and debt footnotes require you to pay above the sticker price.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: With our price-blind audit locked at CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL and PASS_WITH_WATCH, we open the market tape as of the November 20, 2026 close [42, 49]. ABM trades at $53.61 per share within a 52-week range of $36.96 to $55.70 (-3.75% below peak) [49]. Across 58.61 million shares outstanding, equity market value stands at $3.14 billion [49]. Adding roughly $1.77 billion of net debt and lease liabilities yields a $4.91 billion enterprise value [42, 49]. On headline screener ratios, ABM looks modest [49]. The stock trades at 12.35x forward P/E, 9.08x EV/EBITDA, 0.54x EV/Sales, and 10.06x trailing P/FCF, alongside a 2.16% dividend yield ($1.16 annual payout) [49]. Wall Street's consensus target price sits at $55.93 (+4.3% above $53.61) [49].

Our Pass 1 forensic audit exposes why those headline multiples overstate ABM's intrinsic cheapness [42, 47, 49]. First, trailing P/FCF of 10.06x implies ~$312 million of trailing free cash flow [49], yet management's raised FY2026 FCF guidance is only ~$210 million [43]. On $210 million of guided FY2026 FCF, actual P/FCF is 14.95x and EV/FCF is 23.4x [43, 49]. That translates to a 4.28% unlevered FCF yield—sitting 76 basis points below the 5.04% U.S. 10-year Treasury yield [55]. Second, part of the 9M FY2026 operating cash rebound ($275.0 million) coincided with a new $300.0 million Receivables Financing Agreement signed July 28, 2026 ($402.4 million of U.S. receivables pledged), while unbilled contract assets climbed to $518.9 million [42]. Third, June 2026 interest-rate swap expirations left ~86% of $1,778.6 million gross debt floating on SOFR, lifting FY2026 interest guidance to ~$110 million [42]. Fourth, WGNSTAR pushed goodwill and intangibles to $3,069.7 million, creating -$1,279.5 million in negative tangible equity and pinning ROIC at 4.62% against an ~8.8% WACC [42, 49, 55].

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF & Fundamental Fair Value Deconstruction: What $53.61 ($4.91B EV) Prices In
web_blocks.takeaway: At $53.61 ($4.91B EV), ABM already prices in 3.5% organic growth and ~$245M normalized FY27E FCF (~20.0x EV/FCF); even our $56.00 Base Case matches Wall Street's $55.93 consensus and yields only 0.34:1 R:R at CMP (0.53:1 at $52.74 support) against the $46.57 stop.

web_blocks.the_number: Our independent 12-to-18-month Base Case fair value for ABM is $56.00 per share (+4.5% vs. $53.61 CMP), with a probability-weighted expected value of $52.60 (-1.9% vs. CMP) across 20% Bull ($66.00), 50% Base ($56.00), and 30% Bear ($38.00) outcomes.
web_blocks.how_calculated: We value ABM on normalized FY2027E Adjusted EBITDA of $535 million and normalized FY2027E Free Cash Flow of $245 million, deducting $1,770 million of net debt and lease obligations across 58.61 million basic shares. Unlike $1,211.8 million of off-balance-sheet surety bonds, ABM's $584.0 million net self-insurance reserves and $38.7 million earn-outs are on-balance-sheet operating/casualty liabilities excluded from headline net debt. Including 50% of reserves plus earn-outs ($330.7 million) as debt-like across 59.3 million diluted shares drops Bear stress (8.0x on $475M EBITDA) to $28.66, while 20.6x unimproved FY26E FCF ($210M) yields $43.61. Applying 9.44x EV/EBITDA (a modest 0.36x premium to 9.08x, or 20.6x EV/FCF) yields $5,050 million EV and $3,280 million equity ($55.96 per share, rounded to $56.00).
web_blocks.the_inputs: CMP $53.61 (Nov 20, 2026); 58.61M shares; $1.77B net debt (~86% floating SOFR post-June 2026 swap expiry); ~$110M FY26 interest guide; 29%–30% post-WOTC tax rate; ~$210M FY26E FCF guide rising to ~$245M FY27E; 7.7%–7.8% trimmed segment margin; 5.04% U.S. 10-year Treasury yield; 4.62% ROIC.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Case $38.00 (8.4x EV/EBITDA on $475M recessionary EBITDA) to Base Case $56.00 (9.4x EV/EBITDA on $535M EBITDA) to Bull Case $66.00 (9.7x–10.2x EV/EBITDA on $580M EBITDA with deleveraging below 2.5x). Finviz Wall Street consensus target sits at $55.93.
web_blocks.if_off: If ABM retires $250M+ of floating debt without relying on receivables securitization, lifts consolidated FCF sustainably above $275M, and expands ATS/M&D margins back past 8.5%–9.0%, fair value rises toward $66.00. Conversely, if SOFR stays elevated while commercial office attrition cuts EBITDA to $475M, equity value compresses toward $38.00.

web_blocks.caption: ABM Industries vs. Snapshot Industrial Services, Electrical & Commercial Peers (Nov 20, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: ABM carries the lowest EV/EBITDA (9.08x) and forward P/E (12.35x) in this Nov 20 peer cohort, yet its 4.62% ROIC, 4.68% GAAP operating margin, and 6.0% TTM revenue growth trail APi Group (+16.4% growth, 6.7% OPM), Eaton (9.84% ROIC, 19.0% OPM), and BrightSpring (+22.9% growth, 7.58% ROIC).

web_blocks.html: Comparing ABM against the verified November 20 peer snapshot explains why the market caps ABM's multiple [49, 50, 51, 52, 53]. APi Group (APG) operates in life-safety and specialty building services with 16.4% TTM revenue growth and 6.66% operating margin, earning 20.52x forward P/E and 22.60x EV/EBITDA [50]. Eaton (ETN) delivers 18.99% operating margins and 9.84% ROIC in electrical power management, trading at 19.02x forward P/E and 18.90x EV/EBITDA [51]. BrightSpring (BTSG) grows revenue 22.86% with 7.58% ROIC, while Brown & Brown (BRO) earns 29.69% operating margins in commercial brokerage [52, 53]. ABM sits at 9.08x EV/EBITDA and 12.35x forward P/E because 47.2% of revenue still comes from lower-growth Business & Industry contracts, GAAP operating margin is just 4.68%, and WGNSTAR pushed negative tangible book equity to -$1,279.5 million [1, 42, 49].

web_blocks.mechanism: Like ABM, ISS A/S operated a sprawling multi-country janitorial and integrated facility services portfolio weighed down by acquisition goodwill, thin 3%–4% operating margins, heavy IT/ERP spending, and floating-rate debt sensitivity during office occupancy shifts.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: ISS de-rated from ~14x EV/EBITDA in 2017 to 7.5x–8.5x EV/EBITDA across 2020–2023 as organic margins stalled near 3.5%–4.3% and FCF conversion disappointed, re-rating toward ~9.5x–10.5x only after net leverage fell below 2.2x and non-core contracts were exited.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Leveraged facility integrators earning sub-5% ROIC rarely expand past 9.5x–10.5x EV/EBITDA; at 9.08x EV/EBITDA with 86% floating SOFR debt and $210M FY26E FCF, ABM offers almost no valuation cushion at $53.61 [42, 43, 49].

web_blocks.html: Our reward-to-risk arithmetic enforces a clear, non-hedged verdict [49]. At $53.61 CMP against the snapshot invalidation stop of $46.57 ($7.04 per share risk), our $56.00 Base Case offers $2.39 upside—just 0.34:1 reward-to-risk [49]. Even if we wait for a pullback into the snapshot support zone ($51.18–$52.74), buying at $52.74 risks $6.17 to $46.57 for $3.26 upside to $56.00—only 0.53:1 reward-to-risk (or 1.05:1 at $51.18) [49]. Both fall decisively short of our institutional 1.50:1 asymmetry gate. Clearing 1.50:1 from $52.74 support against a $46.57 stop requires at least a $62.00 Base Case fair value, which demands assuming 10.5x EV/EBITDA or $275M+ clean FCF without evidence [42, 43, 49].

web_blocks.caption: EV/EBITDA Sensitivity Matrix: Implied Equity Value per Share (58.61M Shares, $1.77B Net Debt)
web_blocks.takeaway: Because $1.77B of net debt represents 36% of Enterprise Value, ABM needs both $580M+ EBITDA and 9.5x–10.5x multiple expansion to clear $62+; at $535M Base EBITDA and 9.1x–9.5x EV/EBITDA, fair value clusters tightly between $52.87 and $56.52.

web_blocks.html: Finally, ABM's 58-year dividend streak ($1.16 per share, 2.16% yield, ~$68 million annual cash cost) provides modest income support but slows balance-sheet repair [17, 49]. After paying ~$68 million in dividends and ~$80 million in maintenance CapEx out of ~$210 million FY2026E FCF, only ~$142 million remains before buybacks [42, 43]. Because ABM spent $94.7 million repurchasing shares in 9M FY2026 while adding $300 million in receivables financing, net debt stayed elevated [42, 43]. Until management prioritizes retiring floating SOFR debt over M&A and buybacks, valuation upside stays capped near $56.00 [42, 47, 49]. Sensitivity to on-balance-sheet casualty liabilities reinforces caution [42]. Treating 50% of $584.0 million net self-insurance reserves plus $38.7 million earn-outs ($330.7 million) as debt-like on 59.3 million diluted shares cuts Bear stress (8.0x on $475M EBITDA) to $28.66, while 20.6x on unimproved $210 million FY2026E FCF implies $43.61 even before that reserve deduction [42, 43, 49]. Hence, $44.00 is strictly conditional on unsecuritized FCF and deleveraging gates—never a guaranteed valuation floor [42, 43].

What Changes Our Valuation View: We would reopen underwriting only if ABM delivers two quarters of >=$70M unsecuritized FCF, cuts net leverage below 2.4x, and restores ATS/M&D margins above 8.5%, lifting Base fair value above $62.00.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have stripped out every blind spot from Chapters 1 through 6, we open the live market tape as of the November 20, 2026 close. ABM trades at $53.61 per share, down 3.75% from its 52-week high of $55.70, giving the company a $3.14 billion equity market cap across 58.61 million shares. Add roughly $1.77 billion of net debt and lease obligations, and the enterprise value stands at $4.91 billion.

On a surface-level financial screener, ABM looks almost tempting. The stock trades at 12.35x forward earnings, 9.08x trailing EV/EBITDA, 0.54x EV/sales, and 10.06x trailing free cash flow, with a 2.16% dividend yield backed by 58 straight years of dividend increases. Wall Street's average analyst target price sits at $55.93.

But remember what our Pass 1 forensic review uncovered in the SEC footnotes before we ever looked at the stock price. That 10.06x trailing P/FCF ratio is an accounting mirage driven by working-capital timing and a brand-new $300 million accounts-receivable securitization facility signed in late July 2026. Management's actual full-year FY2026 free cash flow guidance is only ~$210 million—which translates to 14.95x P/FCF and 23.4x EV/FCF, or a 4.28% unlevered cash yield when U.S. 10-year Treasuries pay 5.04%.

book_subsections.title: What $53.61 Already Prices In: The Reverse DCF Reality Check
paragraphs: When we invert the cash flow model on $4.91 billion of enterprise value at an 8.8% weighted average cost of capital, $53.61 is not priced for collapse, but it is not cheap either. It already assumes ABM compounds revenue around 3.5% per year, holds GAAP operating margins near 4.8%, and stabilizes free cash flow around $235 million to $250 million in FY2027.

Yet remember the three drags sitting right in front of that cash flow: June 2026 interest-rate swap expirations exposed 86% of ABM's $1.78 billion gross debt to floating SOFR rates (~$110 million interest expense), WOTC hiring tax credits expired at year-end 2025, and unbilled receivables climbed to $518.9 million. Paying 20x normalized FY2027 free cash flow for a 4.62% ROIC business in a 5.04% Treasury world offers no margin of safety.

Let's walk through why the gap between GAAP accounting and Wall Street's adjusted numbers matters so much here. On Finviz, ABM's trailing GAAP earnings are $2.77 per share (19.37x P/E), while forward adjusted earnings are ~$4.34 per share (12.35x forward P/E). Where do those missing $1.57 per share go? They go into $52.5 million+ of recurring intangible amortization from roll-up deals like WGNSTAR, ongoing restructuring charges ($28.0 million cumulative through Q3 FY2026), and stock-based compensation. Pretending those cash acquisition costs don't exist overstates true economic earning power.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Never confuse a low headline P/E ratio with a bargain. When a business carries $3.07 billion of goodwill and intangibles, -$1.28 billion of negative tangible book equity, and 86% floating-rate debt, every dollar of EBITDA has a crowded line of creditors waiting ahead of shareholders.

book_subsections.title: The Footnote Debt Wedge: Receivables Factoring, Insurance Reserves & Swaps
paragraphs: Let's examine three balance-sheet items that a standard screener completely misses when computing ABM's $4.91 billion enterprise value. First, on July 28, 2026, ABM signed a $300.0 million Receivables Financing Agreement and pledged $402.4 million of U.S. customer receivables into a bankruptcy-remote special-purpose entity. That facility was fully drawn at $300.0 million just three days later at quarter-end, boosting liquidity and masking working-capital strain while unbilled receivables sat at $309.1 million and costs in excess of billings hit $209.8 million.

Second, ABM carries $584.0 million of on-balance-sheet net self-insurance casualty and medical reserves ($664.9 million gross casualty plus $9.9 million medical less $90.8 million recoverables) alongside $38.7 million in earn-outs—unlike its $1,211.8 million in off-balance-sheet surety bonds. Over FY2024 and FY2025 alone, ABM absorbed $43.6 million of adverse prior-year casualty reserve adjustments—yet management still excludes those charges when calculating executive cash bonuses.

Third, Note 7 of the Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q reveals that the majority of ABM's interest-rate swaps expired in June 2026, leaving just $248.6 million hedged at 3.68% fixed. Nearly 86% of ABM's $1.78 billion debt load now floats on SOFR ahead of a $1.68 billion maturity wall in FY2029 and FY2030. That single rate shift lifted full-year interest guidance to ~$110 million, consuming more than a third of GAAP operating income.

book_subsections.title: Benchmarking ABM Against November 2026 Snapshot Peers
paragraphs: Looking at our verified November 20 peer snapshot shows exactly why the market refuses to pay 18x or 20x EBITDA for ABM. APi Group in life-safety and specialty building services is growing sales 16.4% at a 6.66% operating margin and commands 22.60x EV/EBITDA. Eaton delivers 18.99% operating margins and 9.84% ROIC in electrical power equipment. BrightSpring is expanding revenue 22.86% with a 7.58% ROIC.

ABM, by contrast, is growing 6.0% on a trailing basis with a 4.68% GAAP operating margin and a 4.62% ROIC, while 47.2% of its business remains anchored in commercial office janitorial contracts. Historically, leveraged European facility roll-up ISS A/S traded between 7.5x and 9.5x EV/EBITDA until it cut leverage below 2.2x. At 9.08x EV/EBITDA today, ABM is priced right where its capital efficiency belongs.

Even Brown & Brown—a commercial services firm in our snapshot cohort—earns nearly 30% operating margins on a capital-light brokerage model. ABM employs 113,000 workers, ~45% of whom are covered by over 300 union collective bargaining agreements alongside a Red-Zone SEIU multiemployer pension plan. That labor structure makes sudden margin expansion extraordinarily difficult.

book_subsections.title: Why Even a Pullback Fails Our 1.50:1 Reward-to-Risk Gate
paragraphs: Here is the decisive math that separates disciplined underwriting from wishful hedging. Using $535 million of FY2027E EBITDA at 9.44x EV/EBITDA—or roughly 20.6x normalized FY2027E FCF of $245 million—gives an independent Base Case fair value of $56.00 per share, virtually identical to Wall Street's $55.93 consensus. Our Bull Case reaches $66.00 if ATS and cleanroom margins rebound above 9% and floating debt comes down, while our Bear Case drops to $38.00 if office attrition and floating SOFR rates squeeze EBITDA toward $475 million.

Weighting those scenarios 20% Bull, 50% Base, and 30% Bear produces a probability-weighted expected value of $52.60—below today's $53.61 share price. Even if you wait patiently for ABM to pull back to the top of its snapshot support band at $52.74 against the $46.57 invalidation stop, you are risking $6.17 per share to make $3.26 to our $56.00 Base Case. That is a 0.53:1 reward-to-risk ratio—not even close to our 1.50:1 institutional threshold. When even the support zone fails 1.50:1, the honest verdict is REJECTED.

Liability-wedge sensitivity reinforces why caution is warranted. ABM's $584.0 million net self-insurance reserves and $38.7 million earn-outs sit on the balance sheet as operating obligations, unlike its $1,211.8 million of off-balance-sheet surety bonds. If an investor treats 50% of those net reserves plus earn-outs ($330.7 million) as debt-like across 59.3 million diluted shares, Bear-case stress (8.0x on $475 million EBITDA) falls to $28.66 per share—and even without that deduction, 20.6x EV/FCF on unimproved $210 million FY2026E FCF yields only $43.61. Consequently, our $44.00 monitor price is conditional on unsecuritized FCF stability and deleveraging gates, never a guaranteed valuation floor.

book_subsections.title: How Floating Debt and Dividends Constrain Deleveraging
paragraphs: One final piece of cash math seals the valuation case. After ABM pays ~$68 million for its 58-year dividend streak out of ~$210 million in FY2026 free cash flow, only ~$142 million remains before any share buybacks or contingent earn-outs for RavenVolt ($32.5 million) and LMC ($5.9 million). Yet through the first nine months of FY2026, management spent $94.7 million buying back stock while pledging $402.4 million of receivables for a $300 million securitization line.

Adding debt to buy back stock in a 5% interest-rate environment while executive performance shares vest 100% on M&A-adjusted EBITDA and revenue with zero ROIC hurdle is a governance red flag. Until free cash flow clears $275 million cleanly without receivables factoring and net leverage drops below 2.4x, we refuse to stretch our multiple above 9.5x EV/EBITDA.

book_subsections.title: How Balance-Sheet Leverage Magnifies Every Turn of the Multiple
paragraphs: Notice how ABM's $1.77 billion net debt load turns even a small change in market sentiment into a wide swing in equity value. Because debt accounts for 36% of ABM's $4.91 billion enterprise value, every 1.0x turn of EV/EBITDA expansion or contraction on $535 million of FY2027E EBITDA shifts equity value by roughly $9.13 per share—nearly 17% of today's $53.61 share price.

That leverage cuts sharply to the downside when macro conditions soften. If commercial office occupancy pressures and rising union wage costs push EBITDA down just 11% to $475 million while the multiple compresses one turn to 8.0x EV/EBITDA, implied equity value drops to $34.64 per share. Conversely, clearing $62 per share requires both $580 million of Bull-Case EBITDA and at least 9.5x EV/EBITDA—an outcome that leaves no margin for error at today's price.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest discipline in value investing is admitting when a prior watchlist thesis breaks under deeper footnote forensics. A $56.00 Base Case against a $46.57 stop offers 0.53:1 asymmetry at support—making REJECTED the only intellectually honest rating.
